Job Description

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Operations Graduate Program – Summer 2027 Internship

What You Will Do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. During this program, you will complete an internship project at Amgen within the Operations function, exploring opportunities and advancing core business priorities. Operations is one of four core functions at Amgen with a mission to manufacture and reliably deliver safe, effective, and high-quality medicine to patients around the world. The organization is spread across ten sites and divided into six functions: Engineering, Global Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Operations Transformation & Digital Strategy, Process Development, and Quality. The graduate internship projects are designed to provide students with the opportunity to solve real organizational challenges and develop essential skills for future career success.

This internship will be approximately 13 weeks, expected to start in the Summer 2027, and includes mentoring, coaching, and experiential learning opportunities to support the development of talent on their continued journey to leadership excellence. Amgen promotes collaboration with senior leadership and other business stakeholders through a series of virtual presentations and networking engagements. Interns are also invited to attend an in-person week at Amgen’s headquarters in Thousand Oaks, CA, which will provide the opportunity for professional development through training sessions, one-on-one mentoring, and multiple networking events.

jobs.title: Agentic Systems Builder & QA Engineer (GB)
jobs.excerpt: About Us Foundever™ is a global leader in the customer experience (CX) industry.
jobs.description:
About Us

Foundever™ is a global leader in the customer experience (CX) industry. With 150,000 associates across the globe, we are the team behind the best experiences for more than 750 of the world's leading and digital-first brands. Our innovative CX solutions, technology, and expertise are designed to support operational needs for our clients and deliver seamless, AI-driven experiences in the moments that matter.

As AI becomes increasingly agentic and autonomous, we are building a platform to orchestrate intelligent workflows that automate complex business processes at scale.

About the role

We are looking for an Agentic Systems Builder & QA Engineer to sit at the intersection of building, testing, and adoption of our agentic systems framework. You will be the first user of the tools we build — stress-testing them, running evaluations, identifying gaps, and feeding insights back to the engineering team.

Beyond QA, you will play a key role in enabling other teams to build with our framework: onboarding them, understanding their use cases, translating their needs into actionable specs, and running discovery to inform the platform roadmap. You will combine hands-on building and testing with product-minded thinking — ensuring that what we ship is not only technically sound but genuinely useful for the teams adopting it.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys working across boundaries: part builder, part tester, part enabler — with a strong sense for what makes tools intuitive, reliable, and ready for real-world use.

Key responsibilities

Building & Testing

  • Be the primary hands-on tester of the agentic systems framework — building agents using our tools, identifying bugs, edge cases, and usability issues before other teams encounter them
  • Run end-to-end evaluations of agentic systems: execute evaluation pipelines, create and curate datasets, analyze results, and report on agent quality and reliability
  • Build and configure agentic workflows using the framework's interfaces — system prompts, model selection, tool integrations — validating that the developer experience works as intended
  • Define and execute QA processes for new framework features, integrations, and releases

Adoption & Enablement

  • Support other technical teams in building agentic systems with our tools — onboarding, troubleshooting, and sharing best practices
  • Act as the bridge between adopting teams and the engineering team: gather feedback, identify friction points, and advocate for improvements
  • Create documentation, guides, and examples that help teams get started and build effectively

Discovery & Product

  • Run discovery with internal teams to understand their use cases, pain points, and requirements for agentic systems
  • Translate user needs into clear specs and requirements that the engineering team can act on
  • Help prioritize framework improvements based on real adoption feedback and observed usage patterns
  • Contribute to roadmap discussions with a grounded perspective on what teams actually need

Evaluation & Quality

  • Execute and refine evaluation workflows — running experiments, comparing agent configurations, and reporting on metrics
  • Help define what "good" looks like for agent behavior in different use cases
  • Flag quality issues, regressions, and drift in deployed agentic systems

Skills / Abilities / Knowledge

Experience
  • 3+ years in a role combining development, QA, testing, or technical product work
  • Experience building or configuring AI/ML-powered systems or applications
  • Experience working directly with end users or internal teams to gather requirements and feedback
  • Some exposure to product management practices: discovery, spec writing, prioritization

Required
  • Comfort working with APIs, configuration interfaces, and developer tooling
  • Understanding of LLMs and how they are integrated into applications (prompting, tool calling, structured outputs)
  • Strong analytical and communication skills — able to clearly articulate issues, feedback, and requirements
  • Detail-oriented with a quality-first mindset
  • Comfortable in Agile, fast-paced environments with evolving scope

Nice to have
  • Experience with agentic systems or agent orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, LangChain, or similar)
  • Experience with observability or evaluation tooling (LangFuse or similar)
  • Experience with MCP Servers/Clients
  • Background in QA engineering or test automation
  • Experience with testing methodologies — manual and/or automated, ideally for AI or non-deterministic systems
  • Experience in a product management or technical product owner role
  • Development skills in Python
  • Familiarity with vector databases, RAG pipelines, or NLP
  • Experience writing technical documentation or developer guides

Education

Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience.

Languages

  • Excellent written and conversational English (C1 minimum)
  • French and Spanish are a plus

Tools & Technologies

LangGraph · LangFuse · MCP Clients & Servers · Python · GitLab · Cursor

Our Offer

  • Impactful work. Opportunity to work on cutting-edge AI technologies that will be game changers for our business.
  • Professional growth. Continuous learning and development opportunities in a dynamic, remote work environment.
  • Competitive compensation. Attractive salary and benefits package.
  • Collaborative environment. A supportive team culture with opportunities for occasional travel for training and industry events.

Speechify’s text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its App of the Day.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

With the growth of our iOS app, being the #18 productivity app in the App Store category and also our recent recognition as Apple's 2025 Design Award for inclusivity, we find the need for a Senior iOS Engineer to help us support the new user base as well as work on new and exciting projects to push our missing forward.

jobs.excerpt: What Do We Do? Triple Whale is the AI operating system built for modern ecommerce.
jobs.description:
What Do We Do?

Triple Whale is the AI operating system built for modern ecommerce. We help you see what's actually working in your business, what's not, and what to do next. Then we take action for you — pausing the underperforming ad, generating the next batch of creative, flagging the inventory risk before it bites.

We pull every signal in your business into one place, and put it on the most trusted measurement foundation in the industry. And on top of that, we give you the most actionable AI in commerce — Moby — letting you tap any LLM you want, grounded in the full context of your business. Moby 2 doesn't just surface insights, it executes decisions for you, with automations that make the rest of your stack smarter.

The result: more than 65,000 brands like Pressed Juicery, OUAI, and True Classic turn mountains of complex data into actions that actually grow profit, at a speed and scale that is not humanly possible.

What You’re Applying for:

We’re looking for an Implementation Manager, Mid-Market to lead the onboarding journey for new Triple Whale customers. The role is equal parts consultative and coordinative. You’ll quickly understand what each customer is actually trying to accomplish, then drive the people, sequencing, and detail that get them there — owning their launch from contract signature through full go-live.

It is hands-on, technical, and has genuine volume behind it. You’ll run a full slate of implementations at once, which means getting very good at making a repeatable process work without any single customer feeling like they are on a conveyor belt. You’ll configure and validate the measurement foundation, be accountable for the accuracy of what the customer sees on day one, and be among the first people to onboard customers onto Moby, our AI agent — teaching teams to run AI-led workflows and automations rather than just read dashboards.

You’ll help set the standard of what good looks like for Mid-market onboarding.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead consultative discovery with new customers — clarify business objectives, surface constraints, and translate desired outcomes into the success criteria you drive toward during onboarding.
  • Own end-to-end delivery for a high-volume book of Mid-Market implementations, from kickoff through go-live and into the handoff to Customer Success — adapting how you run each onboarding to the customer’s goals and setup while protecting speed to value.
  • Configure the technical foundation of each launch — tracking and pixel implementation, platform integrations (Shopify, Meta, Google, Klaviyo, Amazon, and more), and data source connections.
  • Advise on customer tech stacks and recommend integration best practices, with enough API and webhook fluency to know what is possible — and to pull in Solutions Architecture early when a launch genuinely needs custom work.
  • Validate attribution and data accuracy before go-live — and when something looks wrong, describe it precisely enough that Support and Product can act on it, and clearly enough that the customer knows what it means for them.
  • Onboard customers onto Moby, Triple Whale’s AI agent, so teams leave onboarding running AI-led workflows and automations that make the rest of their stack smarter.
  • Run training and enablement — one-to-one where it matters, one-to-many where it scales — to drive adoption and confidence in the platform.
  • Own the handoff to Customer Success: document what was configured, what the customer is measuring, what adoption looks like at go-live, and what remains open, so the CSM starts from a real baseline rather than a blank page.
  • Influence the stakeholders you do not manage — build the internal champion, get the right people to show up, and move a stalled customer team without formal authority.
  • Apply structured risk management across a large book — identify exposure early, mitigate it deliberately, and escalate with a recommendation rather than a problem.
  • Monitor implementation health across your entire portfolio, balancing speed to value against quality and protecting both.
  • Keep project tooling, documentation, and account records current without being reminded.
  • Partner proactively with Customer Success, Product, Support, and Marketing to resolve issues and streamline the path to launch.
  • Spot the patterns across your book and turn them into better onboarding standards — kickoff structure, handoff criteria, templates, and what “done” actually means.

What You’ll Bring

  • 2–4+ years in implementation, onboarding, technical account management, or customer success at a SaaS company.
  • A consultative instinct — you ask about the business problem before reaching for the configuration screen.
  • Strong project management skills — you plan the work, sequence dependencies, and deliver a high volume of concurrent projects on time, without dropping details and without close supervision.
  • Enough technical fluency to be credible: you understand tracking and pixel implementation, integrations, APIs and webhooks well enough to explain what is happening, what it means for the customer, and what has to happen next — without needing someone to translate it for you.
  • Working knowledge of the martech and ecommerce stack — Shopify, Meta and Google Ads, email and SMS platforms — and how attribution actually behaves across them.
  • The ability to balance technical depth with clarity: you can go deep with an analyst, then explain the same thing to a founder without losing either of them.
  • Proven ability to influence stakeholders you have no authority over — you can hold a customer team to their commitments and re-engage one that has gone quiet.
  • Comfort working from a repeatable playbook, and the judgment to know when a customer needs something off-script.
  • Disciplined risk management: you spot exposure early and act on it rather than reporting it.
  • Curiosity about AI and a willingness to teach customers a new way of working, not just a new piece of software.
  • Knowledge of retail and eCommerce business needs, processes, and best practices.
  • An interest in improving how the team works, not just running your own book.

Bonus Points For

  • Previous experience in SaaS, MarTech, analytics, or eCommerce platforms.

Our Values

About Curology:

Curology’s mission is to make effective, personalized skincare accessible. We were founded by dermatologists who believe everyone should have access to skincare products that actually work. Today, our licensed dermatology providers have helped millions of patients across all 50 states make that mission a reality.

We combine expert medical care with personalized prescription formulas and dermatologist-developed skincare essentials to deliver science-backed solutions that meet people where they are. Join us in our mission to transform skin health and enhance lives—one patient at a time.

Mission of the Role:

The mission of the Senior Data Analyst is to turn ambiguous business questions into analytics solutions that inform decisions — owning the work end to end, from problem framing through delivery and adoption. Reporting to the Analytics Lead, this role sits on the Data Analytics team and partners directly with stakeholders across the business.

Success depends on partnering with stakeholders to define the real question behind a request, recommend the right approach, and deliver visualizations and narratives that make the answer usable by non-technical audiences. The Senior Data Analyst connects each analysis to the broader business context rather than answering questions in isolation, and is accountable for the accuracy, documentation, and durability of what they ship.

Essential Functions and Impact Areas:

Stakeholder Consultation & Problem Framing

  • Partner with business stakeholders across Finance, Commercial, Marketing, and Product functional groups to translate open-ended questions into scoped analytical problems with defined success criteria.
  • Ask the follow-up questions that surface the decision behind the request, and push back when the requested output will not answer it.
  • Recommend the analytical approach, including when a request warrants a reusable data asset rather than a one-off pull.
  • Set expectations on scope and timeline, and communicate changes as work progresses.

End-to-End Project Ownership

  • Own analytics projects from intake through delivery and adoption without requiring day-to-day direction.
  • Source, validate, and model data in SQL to produce analysis-ready datasets.
  • Document methodology, assumptions, and known limitations so results can be reproduced and reused.
  • Build analytical assets that compound — reusable datasets, dashboards, and metric definitions rather than disposable outputs.
  • Verify results against source systems before delivery, and surface discrepancies rather than reconciling them silently.

Data Visualization & Storytelling

  • Design Tableau dashboards that answer a defined question for a defined audience, prioritizing clarity over comprehensiveness.
  • Translate analysis into a clear narrative — what the data shows, what it means, and what decision it supports — calibrating depth to non-technical and senior audiences.
  • Distinguish findings from interpretation and state confidence levels explicitly.

Business Context & Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Help elevate the analytics function at Curology by supporting leadership with the insights they need to manage the business and measure outcomes.
  • Connect analysis to how the broader business operates across patients, subscription lifecycle, and downstream financial impact.
  • Partner with data engineering, analytics peers, and business teams to align on metric definitions and prevent duplicate sources of truth.
  • Surface risks and opportunities stakeholders have not asked about.
  • Handle patient and business data in line with Curology’s privacy and security standards.

Requirements

Required Qualifications:

  • 5+ years in an analytics role delivering analysis directly to business stakeholders.
  • Advanced SQL, including complex joins, window functions, and query optimization against large datasets in a cloud data warehouse (Snowflake, Redshift, or similar).
  • Tableau experience building and maintaining production dashboards used by business teams, not one-off visuals.
  • Track record of owning analytics projects end to end, translating ambiguous business questions into a defined approach and recommending the method rather than executing a specified request.
  • Experience defining KPIs and developing metrics, scorecards, and performance reporting used by business teams and leadership.
  • Experience with customer behavior analysis — retention, churn, cohort, and LTV — and defining segmentation used across analytics and reporting.
  • Ability to communicate technical findings to non-technical audiences in both written and live formats.
  • Proficiency using AI as an execution partner to accelerate query drafts, design mockups, and polish outputs, while remaining fully capable of producing the work without AI. Corrects AI output and owns the quality of what ships.

Nice-to-Haves:

  • Experience in a DTC subscription business.
  • Experience supporting lifecycle or CRM marketing teams.
  • Familiarity with email and SMS performance metrics and campaign measurement.

Benefits

Location:

  • Remote (US)

Benefits & Perks:

  • 💰 Competitive compensation and equity package (RSUs)
  • 🥼 Comprehensive benefits: Medical, dental, vision, FSA and HSA, supplemental coverages (critical illness, accident, hospitalization), and 401(k)
  • 🧘🏻‍♀️ Access to wellbeing perks, including OneMedical, Spring Health, SoFi, and Employee Assistance Program
  • 🌴 Flexible paid time off and holiday policy
  • 🐣 Paid parental leave (birthing and non-birthing parents)
  • 💜 Employee donation matching program
  • 🫱🏻‍🫲🏽 Culture Committee and employee resource groups for virtual and in-person connectivity
  • ✨ Complimentary VIP Subscription to Curology or Agency, plus online retail discount

The estimated base salary range for this role is $130,000 – $160,000 per year, plus a competitive equity package and benefits. Actual compensation will be determined based on several factors, including location, skills, experience, and job-related expertise.

Our Typical Interview Process*:

*Subject to change based on role

  • 30 minute Recruiter screen (phone)
  • 30-45 minute interview with a Hiring Manager (Google Meet or Zoom)
  • 30-45 minute technical assessment, case study, or peer interview(s) (Google Meet or Zoom)
  • 30-45 minute final round interview with Hiring Manager or Team Leader (Google Meet or Zoom)

Candidates Using AI:

At Curology, we invest in responsible use of AI tools to help our teams innovate and solve challenges. Please feel free to use AI to:

  • Refine and polish your application materials
  • Research Curology and the role
  • Prepare for your interviews

Please refrain from using AI tools during live interviews, unless our hiring team has instructed you otherwise. (Note: These guidelines do not apply to reasonable accommodations. If you require a reasonable accommodation at any point during our interview process, please notify your recruiter.)

Curology’s Operating Principles:

  • One Curology, One Team
  • Be Candid, Then Commit
  • Lead with Curiosity
  • Trust but Verify
  • Use Peripheral Vision
  • Move Quickly, Think Deeply

POSITION TITLE:IT Support Team Lead

Supervised by: IT Operations Manager

Supervises: IT Support Team Members

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt / Full-Time

POSITION SUMMARY. MediQuant helps more than 250 health systems and hospital networks retire, secure, and modernize their legacy healthcare data. As IT Support Team Lead, you own the frontline experience for every employee and client who depends on MediQuant’s systems working — and working securely.

The IT Support Team Lead owns the day-to-day performance, responsiveness, and service quality of MediQuant’s IT Support function — service desk operations, the ITSM platform, and end-user technology across the business. This role leads the IT Support Team, sets support standards and processes, and partners closely with the IT Operations Manager on roadmap, staffing, and service-level commitments.

JOB DUTIES and ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS. A qualified individual must be able to perform these essential functions of the job as listed, with or without accommodation.

  1. Service Desk Operations & Incident Management
    1. Owns day-to-day service desk operations, planning, and execution for MediQuant’s IT Support function — both internal and client-facing.
    2. Manages escalated incidents through to resolution; documents root cause and resolution in knowledge base articles for future reference.
    3. Establishes staff working schedules and task allocation to ensure coverage aligned with contractual and client SLA/OLA requirements.
    4. Monitors and reports on services and service levels, operating within the SLAs/OLAs negotiated by the IT Operations Manager.
    5. Ensures the team maintains on-call/escalation coverage, escalating unresolved gaps to the IT Operations Manager.
  2. ITSM Platform, Documentation & Training
    1. Manages and administers the ITSM/ticketing platform SolarWinds Service Desk, including workflows, knowledge base articles, and reporting.
    2. Maintains and updates dashboards for system health and ITSM metrics using existing templates and tooling.
    3. Ensures documentation and knowledge articles for recurring incidents, support procedures, and automation tooling are created and maintained.
    4. Develops staff ability to co-manage the ITSM platform; leads the team in developing training materials and onboarding documentation for support processes.
  3. Compliance & Data Security
    1. Ensures data integrity, access controls, and secure handling of Confidential Data and PHI across all systems and support interactions under this role’s oversight.
    2. Executes HIPAA compliance controls relevant to the IT Support function, including evidence collection supporting MediQuant’s HITRUST r2 certification. The IT Operations Manager holds operational compliance accountability; the Information Security Manager holds final compliance program ownership and audit sign-off.
    3. Partners with Security/Compliance leadership on audit readiness, risk assessments, and remediation tracking for support-related findings.
  4. Projects & Portfolio Governance
    1. Provides input into IT Support-domain project plans — resourcing needs, timeline risks, and dependencies — and functions as a project resource on cross-functional IT projects when support expertise is required. Flags risk or slippage on owned initiatives to the IT Operations Manager.
    2. Coordinates with the PMO/project management function on schedule and dependencies for support-related initiatives.
    3. Independently verifies the actual state of support systems, tickets, and initiatives owned by this role, rather than relying solely on team- or vendor-reported status.
    4. Proactively escalates risk, slippage, or emerging issues to the IT Operations Manager in advance of impact, with a recommended course of action.
    5. Develops and evolves the IT Support services roadmap in partnership with the IT Operations Manager, aligning with the Infrastructure & Database Team Lead on shared platforms and dependencies.
  5. Stakeholder Service & Process Improvement
    1. Leads the support service approval process.
    2. Ensures service awareness across all client onboarding activities, production deployments, and Go-Live support.
    3. Ensures customer service excellence by monitoring tickets, reviewing customer feedback, and driving continuous improvement of the support experience.
    4. Partners with HR, Implementation Services, Sales, or other business functions, as directed by the IT Operations Manager, to document new operational workflows that touch IT Support systems or tooling.
  6. Team Leadership & Performance Management
    1. Builds 30-60-90-day onboarding plans and conducts onboarding one-on-ones for new hires; provides input for their early (90-day) performance review.
    2. Holds regular one-on-ones and conducts performance reviews at agreed intervals (90-day, semi-annual, annual) against competency standards set by Technology Leadership; the IT Operations Manager holds final accountability for ratings, salary discussions, and issuance.
    3. Builds a day-to-day learning environment; identifies and nominates staff for training, coursework, and certifications. The IT Operations Manager approves and funds training and certification investment.
    4. Manages timekeeping and leave administration for direct reports, including approval of timecards, PTO, and schedule adjustments to maintain operational coverage and payroll accuracy.
    5. Interviews and evaluates candidates and recommends hire/no-hire decisions, partnering with Human Resources throughout; the IT Operations Manager holds final hiring sign-off.
    6. Recommends performance ratings and Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs) to the IT Operations Manager for sign-off, and implements approved PIPs and other approved personnel actions.
  7. Team Resourcing & Succession
    1. Owns daily task, shift, and queue allocation to meet coverage and delivery commitments for the team.
    2. Identifies and closes cross-training and skill-gap coverage needs within the team.
    3. Translates IT Operations Manager-set team goals into day-to-day priorities and assignments.
    4. Provides input on intra-team staffing and FTE allocation; the IT Operations Manager owns final allocation decisions.
    5. Recommends succession candidates and escalates staffing or resourcing risk to the IT Operations Manager.

QUALIFICATIONS

Competencies:

  • Critical Thinking
  • Technical Acumen — IT Support & ITSM
  • Professionalism and Composure
  • Interpersonal and Communication Skills
  • Flexibility and Self-Motivation
  • Documentation Skills
  • Team Leadership and Coaching

Required Education and Experience:

  • Associate degree (or actively pursuing) in a technical field of study, with certificates in a computer-related field, or equivalent work experience.
  • 3+ years of IT support/service desk experience, including 1+ years in a lead or supervisory capacity.
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA regulations involving PHI.

About Engine

Engine is the all-in-one travel and spend management platform trusted by 38K+ businesses and groups representing 1.8M+ travelers. We're the retailer and the rails of business travel, the fastest-growing company in travel tech, built on a decade of proprietary technology, supply, and pricing no one else can replicate. Other travel and AI companies run on our infrastructure to book real trips, hold rates, and move payments, without building any of it themselves. We built it, AI-forward at every layer, from how travelers book to how the rails run.

That work has earned recognition as one of Fast Company's Best Workplaces for Innovators (2025), TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020–2026).

We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar.

Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us.

About the Role

We're looking for a Director of Groups & Events to lead our Groups Contracts and Groups Bookings teams. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who thrives in the details as much as in the strategy — someone who doesn't just oversee the work but genuinely understands it, can step into it, and uses that proximity to make the team and the customer experience meaningfully better every day.

You'll own the end-to-end support experience for group travel, from contract management through booking execution, and you'll bring the rare combination of operational depth, people leadership, and strategic clarity that this function requires. You know the workflows. You know where the friction lives. And you build the systems, the culture, and the team capability to eliminate it.

At Engine, we don't aim to meet industry benchmarks — we aim to make the industry benchmark against us. This role is for someone who holds themselves and their team to that standard.

What You'll Do

Lead and develop the Groups Contracts and Groups Bookings teams. You own performance, culture, and day-to-day operations across both teams. You develop your managers and leads with directness and intention — giving real feedback, building real capability, and creating the conditions for people to do the best work of their careers. The leaders who come up under you go on to run their own functions.

Be a player/coach and power user. You don't manage from a distance. You maintain deep, current working knowledge of end-to-end group handling — from initial inquiry and contract execution through booking confirmation and post-travel support. You can pull up a contract, work a complex case, navigate the systems your team uses every day, and identify exactly where the experience breaks down. Your proximity to the work is not occasional — it's how you lead. When a high-stakes situation arises, you're in it, not watching from the sidelines.

Drive continuous improvement relentlessly. You use data and direct observation to find problems before customers report them. You build feedback loops — from QA audits to coaching sessions to SOP rewrites to retraining cycles — and you close them. You don't flag issues and wait for someone else to fix them. You identify the root cause, build the solution, and measure whether it worked. Process improvement isn't a project for you — it's an operating mode.

Own the operational metrics. Establish baselines, track performance, and hold the team accountable to clear and measurable outcomes — booking conversion rate, L90 median timing, QA scores, SLA performance, and client satisfaction. You know which numbers matter, what's driving them, and what it takes to move them.

Manage BPO vendor performance. You have experience running BPO partnerships and you bring that discipline to the Groups function. You hold external partners to Engine's quality standards — not theirs — and you know the difference between a vendor that needs coaching and a vendor that needs accountability. You manage performance cadences, escalate when the bar isn't being met, and work with the OpEx Vendor Manager on contracts and transitions. You've been on the ground with a BPO partner and you know what good looks like at the agent level, not just the reporting level.

Be the senior escalation point. For complex group contracts, high-stakes client situations, and cross-functional issues that require experienced judgment — you're the person who gets the call. You resolve with speed and confidence, you document what happened and why, and you use every escalation as an input into making the system better.

Partner cross-functionally. Work closely with Sales, Account Management, and Finance to ensure group programs are set up for success and clients are supported throughout the lifecycle. You're not a handoff point — you're a genuine partner who brings operational insight into commercial conversations and vice versa.

Contribute to the broader Member Support strategy. Bring a groups-specific lens to decisions that affect the wider organization. You're a peer on the leadership team, not just a functional operator — and you use that seat to make Client Ops better across the board.

What We're Looking For

You are customer obsessed — operationally, not rhetorically. You read case transcripts. You sit with agents. You've called a hotel on behalf of a client to understand what the experience actually feels like on the other end. You treat friction in the customer journey as a personal problem to solve, and you build teams that feel the same way. For you, customer obsession isn't a value on a wall — it's visible in every process decision you make.

You are a true player/coach. You lead by modeling. You're not above rolling up your sleeves, working a complex group contract, or jumping on a call with a client when it matters. You set the standard by demonstrating it — and your team follows because they've seen you do the work, not just talk about it. At the same time, you know when to zoom out, when to delegate, and how to build the management layer that scales without you.

You have deep contact center and BPO management experience. You've run operations with BPO partners at meaningful scale — vendor selection, performance management, commercial negotiations, quality calibration, and transitions. You know how to get the best out of a BPO relationship and when to escalate. You've managed 24/7 or extended-hours operations and built the shift structures, coverage models, and escalation protocols that keep them running.

You are a continuous improvement practitioner. You've implemented process improvement frameworks — Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent — and you've seen them produce real, measurable outcomes. You don't accept "that's how we've always done it." You build feedback loops that actually close.

You develop people intentionally. Your direct reports get better under you. You give clear, direct feedback, invest in development, and build teams that are both high-performing and resilient. You're known for producing managers and leaders, not just executing tasks.

You set standards, you don't chase them. Industry benchmarks are a starting point, not a destination. You have strong opinions about what great looks like in group travel support, you build toward it with urgency, and you hold the line when the pressure is to cut corners.

Experience & Qualifications

  • 12+ years in travel operations, group travel support, or a closely related field — with at least 5 years in a director-level or senior leadership role
  • Hands-on expertise with group travel bookings and contract management — you understand the operational complexity because you've lived it
  • Proven BPO management experience — vendor performance management, quality standards enforcement, commercial negotiations, and operational transitions
  • A track record of driving measurable improvement in team performance, process efficiency, and customer satisfaction
  • Strong people leadership — you develop talent, give direct feedback, and build teams that are both high-performing and resilient
  • Experience operating at multiple altitudes — from reviewing a contract detail to presenting a quarterly operational review to senior leadership
  • Strong cross-functional communication skills with experience partnering with Sales, Account Management, and Finance
  • High attention to detail and strong operational instincts — you notice what's broken before it becomes a problem
  • Experience in a fast-paced, high-growth environment where the playbook is still being written

Bonus Points

  • Experience with GDS platforms (Travelport, Sabre, or similar) in a groups or corporate travel context
  • Background in building or scaling a groups support function from the ground up
  • Familiarity with RFP management, room block logistics, or hotel commission tracking
  • Experience designing or operating a premium or tiered support model
  • Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent process improvement credential

We're building something genuinely different in the travel industry — and the Groups function is one of the most visible and commercially meaningful ways we deliver on that. This role has real scope, real visibility, and a genuine opportunity to shape how Engine supports one of the more complex and high-touch parts of our business. You'll inherit a team that's already executing well — and have the mandate, the resources, and the executive support to take it to the next level. If you want to lead a function, build the standard, and make something meaningfully better — this is the role.

Applications for this role will be accepted through December 31st, 2026 or until the role is filled. We encourage you to apply early, as we may begin reviewing applications before the deadline.

Compensation
Our compensation packages are based on several factors, including your experience, expertise, and location. In addition to a competitive base salary, total compensation may include equity and/or variable pay (OTE). Your recruiter will share your complete compensation package as you move through the process.

Perks and benefits may vary based on employment type, location, and more.

Vote-USA.org informs and educates voters by producing comprehensive, nonpartisan election information for national, state, and many local elections. A longtime partner of VoteUSA, WeVote is a nonpartisan, volunteer-powered civic‑tech nonprofit and a Fast Forward nonprofit technology grantee. jobs.title: Sr Product Manager of Integrations
jobs.excerpt: KarmaCheck is the leader in modern background checks and screenings for the staffing industry, pushing the boundaries of workflow automation.
jobs.description:
KarmaCheck is the leader in modern background checks and screenings for the staffing industry, pushing the boundaries of workflow automation. Our customers work in ATS, VMS, and HRIS platforms which utilize our integrations and API to run screening, verification, and credentialing workflows without switching systems.
We are building an AI workforce: agents that automate the compliance workflows our customers run. Those products reach their full value when they show up inside the systems our customers already use. Building an agent in our own dashboard is the first half of the work. Getting it into Bullhorn, Symplr CTM, Workday, or a customer's proprietary system is the unlock.
This role owns that unlock, alongside additional workflow automation development, and the day-to-day integration products our customers depend on. The ideal hire can commit to working Eastern Time (EST).

The surface you would own

  • Pre-built ATS, HRIS, and HCM integrations: Bullhorn, where KarmaCheck selects required checks based on job placement specifications and writes completed screenings back to the candidate record. KarmaCheck is the only background check integration in Bullhorn's investment portfolio. Symplr CTM, where teams order screenings, sync candidate data, and download completed documents directly from the candidate profile. Workday, delivering background check history, status updates, and results into the candidate's Workday record. WIth additional integrations existing and to come.
  • Service and technology partners: An ecosystem spanning VMS and direct sourcing providers, currently including Conexis, Simpliant, Bridge, Shiftrx, Livehire, Renhead, and Opus Match, supported by revenue-share and referral programs.
  • Public API: An API-first architecture where customers have access to the same calls we use thousands of times a day, with a deliberately broad endpoint surface, customer-mapped data fields, automated consumer report delivery, and support for most ATS, HRIS, HCM, and VMS platforms as well as homegrown systems.

What you will own

  • Taking what we build to market, technically. This is the part of the job that makes it more than integration creation and maintenance. As we release AI agents and new screening products, you own how they reach customers inside their own systems: what the integration story is for each one, which partner surfaces it needs to land on, what has to change in the API or the partner integration to support it, and how a customer actually turns it on. You will work in tandem with the product managers driving AI and new product development.
  • Integration product and partnerships. Ongoing ownership of the Bullhorn, Symplr CTM, and Workday integrations, the partner ecosystem, and whatever we take on next. You will define what integrating with KarmaCheck means: which data flows, how statuses map, how errors surface, what we standardize and where we accommodate a partner's model. You will work directly with partner product and engineering teams and own the roadmap for each integration rather than treating it as a one-time build.
  • Customer-facing implementation and scoping. You will be in front of customers regularly: integration discovery and solutions on new deals, scoping sessions during implementation, and the calls where a customer describes a workflow we do not yet support. Enterprise deals in healthcare staffing almost always hinge on an integration, and you will be the product voice in those conversations.
  • API and developer experience. Our public API and documentation are part of the product and often the first thing a technical buyer evaluates. You will own how they evolve in partnership with engineering: endpoint and webhook design, versioning and deprecation, error semantics, sandbox and testing experience, and documentation quality.
  • Support for Implementation and Support teams. Configuration and tooling that let Implementation stand up an integration without engineering involvement, clear enablement for Support, and a discipline of turning recurring issues into roadmap items rather than repeat manual fixes. The goal is that each launch requires less of Product and Engineering than the one before it.

The requirements we're looking for

  • 5+ years in product management, with meaningful time owning integrations, APIs, or platform products
  • Integration experience across multiple different systems. We care more about the breadth of patterns you have seen than about any one platform. If you arrive with strong instincts about how integrations should be built, mapped, versioned, and supported, you will be useful on day one
  • Direct experience owning partner or API integrations as an ongoing product rather than a project. You have made standardize-versus-accommodate calls and lived with the consequences
  • Genuine comfort in front of customers, including when the goal is to sell. You will demo products, communicate value, and position our capability from a place of strength with technical buyers and operations leaders, then stay with that customer through discovery, scoping, and implementation. Much of what moves deals in this business is carried by product people, and you will be one of them.
  • Technical fluency to work directly with engineers on APIs, webhooks, data models, and error handling. You do not need to be an engineer, but you should never need a translator
  • Ability to turn input from customers, partners, and internal teams into clear, written, prioritized requirements
  • Comfort working with external partner teams, including the diplomacy of influencing a roadmap you do not control

Helpful, and learnable here

  • Healthcare staffing, background screening, credentialing, or compliance. Domain depth matters in this business, but we would rather hire strong integration instincts and ramp the domain than the reverse
  • Credentialing or verification experience, particularly locum tenens/physicians, which is a direction we are moving
  • Familiarity with ATS, VMS, HCM, or HRIS ecosystems such as Bullhorn, Symplr, or Workday
  • Developer experience or API product work
  • Experience bringing AI or automation features into third-party systems

Serving as the Executive liaison to senior corporate and philanthropic leaders, the VP partners with members as a trusted advisor. They bring discernment, commercial rigor, and creativity to shape high-impact experiences aligned to each member’s strategic priorities. This role blends strategic judgment with hands-on execution and is ideal for a leader who thrives at the intersection of relationship depth, business outcomes, and mission-driven work.

With strong executive presence, a refined servicing philosophy, and a proven track record owning and/or contributing towards renewals and expansion, this leader helps elevate both the member experience and NationSwell’s long-term revenue durability.

Location: Remote (must be based in the United States).

Key Responsibilities

New Membership

  • Build Pipeline and Win New Institutional Members - Build and nurture a business development pipeline and prospect list for an assigned territory or segment, leveraging personal network along with outbound support and other engagement tactics, to grow NationSwell's Institutional Membership base.

  • Leverage Network to Build Pipeline - Leverage an established network of senior leaders across corporate, philanthropic, and social impact organizations to build relationships with key stakeholders and prospective members in target segments, converting prospects into members.

Membership Growth, Retention, and Servicing

  • Own UR, NRR and Growth Goals – Hold ultimate accountability for Unit Renewal and Net Revenue Retention across a portfolio of high-value members. Drive organic growth through expanded engagement, cross-sell and upsell opportunities, and executive referrals, with a clear point of view on commercial prioritization and account potential.
  • Oversee Strategic Account Servicing - Serve as the primary strategic owner for each account, developing tailored servicing strategies that align NationSwell’s offerings to members’ evolving business, impact, and leadership priorities. Bring structured thinking and sound judgment to identify opportunities, anticipate risks, and guide members toward high-value engagement across membership, Studio, and programming offerings.
  • Coach and Mentor Member Success partners - Coach and mentor Member Success partners, modeling best-in-class enterprise servicing behaviors, executive presence, and commercial discipline. Establish high standards for account planning, renewal strategy, documentation, and member communication.

Drive Best-in-Class Member Experience

  • Shape Responsive Programming - Partner closely with the Executive Team and cross-functional leaders to inform and refine programming, ensuring experiences are relevant, rigorous, and responsive to member priorities. Translate member insight into actionable input for product, programming, and Studio work.
  • Facilitate Member Events – Confidently facilitate in-person and virtual convenings with senior leaders. Bring presence, warmth, and discernment to create trusted spaces for dialogue, insight-sharing, and peer connection.
  • Build Community – Actively foster peer-to-peer connection and collaboration across the NationSwell community, helping members build meaningful relationships that extend beyond individual events or programs.

Requirements

  • 10+ years of experience in enterprise business development and/or account management, customer success, strategic partnerships, or consulting roles, with direct ownership of sales and renewals, and ownership of expansion goals for a portfolio of complex accounts.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop new partnerships and meet new business revenue targets, in addition to expansion and renewal ownership.
  • Experience developing go-to-market strategies for new segments or territories.
  • Established network of senior-level leaders across corporate social impact/CSR, philanthropic, and social sector organizations, with demonstrated ability to activate that network for both new business development and account growth.
  • Proven ability to operate as a trusted advisor to C-suite and senior executives, drawing on existing relationships and bringing sound judgment, discretion, and strategic insight.
  • Highly developed executive presence. Comfortable navigating ambiguity, influencing without authority, and engaging senior leaders with confidence and credibility.
  • Strong facilitation and convening skills, with the ability to read dynamics, elevate dialogue, and create inclusive, high-quality experiences.
  • Experience building, refining, and/or executing servicing motions, tools, or playbooks. Brings a point of view on what best-in-class servicing looks like.
  • Confident and proven people management skills, ideally within account servicing teams.
  • Commercially minded and metrics-driven, with comfort operating against revenue goals and using data to inform decisions.
  • Collaborative leadership style: works seamlessly with cross-functional partners (Member Success, Studio, Growth) to deliver one unified experience.
  • High motor, entrepreneurial orientation, and comfort operating with cross-functional partners (Member Success, Studio, Business Development) in a fast-growing, evolving organization.
  • Facility with Salesforce or other CRM, preferred; must be skilled at learning new systems and maintaining tight documentation.
  • Experience working with corporate social impact/CSR, philanthropic, or mission-driven organizations strongly preferred.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Distinguished Architect - Security

Job Location: Work at Home, Connecticut, United States

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full time

Job Seniority Level:

We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

We are seeking a highly experienced and technically skilled Distinguished Architect specializing in security to help drive our technology organization’s future strategy. This role will require a deep understanding of the application of security to business applications. The successful candidate will be responsible for architecting security reference architectures that meet the needs of the broader technology organization.

We are seeking a Distinguished Architect who:

  • Possesses significant (IC) leadership experience and has driven large technical initiatives across an enterprise in an influencing role.
  • Is deeply passionate about security with significant (deep and broad) experience in these areas.
  • Can dive deep into the details of how secure solutions but also can communicate a broader vision.
  • Has worked in a broad architecture role in a large enterprise with a very complex technology landscape.
  • Builds strong relationships and is highly collaborative with others.

What you will do:

  • Be part of a team responsible for enabling secure technology solutions that meets our business strategy and drives business value.
  • Define and collaborate on the creation of security roadmaps, security reference architectures, standards, best practice documents, and secure-by-design reference implementations that accelerate delivery while ensuring safety and compliance.
  • Evaluate market trends in cybersecurity, execute buy vs. build decisions and assess cost and the risk impact on targeted business outcomes.
  • Define future state security architecture that supports secure adoption of Artificial Intelligence, APIs, data stores, cloud infrastructures, cloud services, and microservices.
  • Collaborate and consult with technology, cybersecurity, and business partners to optimize business applications and systems that adopt modern and secure architectures, especially around AI.
  • Develop and maintain a strategic vision for the secure use of AI technologies, aligned to the CVS Health platform based on key business drivers, regulatory requirements, and emerging threat trends.
  • Define and collaborate on the creation of security frameworks for the enterprise that promote reuse, reduces cost, manages risk, and increases speed to market.
  • Effectively build and maintain strong relationships with technology, cybersecurity, and business partners to establish trust and influence key security decisions.
  • Provide guidance, direction and mentorship to engineers and other stakeholders regarding security architecture and secure design of enterprise applications.
  • Ensure all Non-Functional Security Requirements (e.g., authentication, authorization, resilience, encryption, auditability, availability, etc.) are properly articulated, and work with all parties to guarantee that delivered software products meet these objectives.
  • Participates in high-level security estimation and security evaluation of AI-enabled solutions.
  • Mentor and coach junior architects and seek the opportunity to bring continuous improvement in secure engineering and enterprise security practices.
  • Strategize and outline long-term security architectural plans for a complex technology environment.

Required Qualifications:

  • 15+ years of relevant work experience (10+ years in technical security leadership roles)
  • 10+ years of experience building or securing large-scale business applications using modern technologies and architectural patterns.
  • 10+ years of experience designing secure integrations with a focus on performance, resilience, and loose coupling using APIs, microservices, and event-driven architecture.
  • Evidence of significant contributions in previous roles and/or to the broader industry.
  • Expert-level understanding of security architectural methodologies/best practices, regulatory and compliance requirements, and risk frameworks that influence architecture decisions.
  • Recognized technical leader with full stack technology knowledge and recognized as an expert in multiple security domains such as: Identity & access management (IAM), network security, cloud security (AWS/Azure/GCP), data protection, zero trust, or security operations.
  • Experience recognizing the impact security architecture decisions can have on strategic business decisions.
  • Substantial experience with requirements analysis, risk assessment, estimation, and secure application design.
  • Expert understanding of architectural governance, security design patterns, AI safety controls, secure development standards, and best practices.
  • A diverse technical background with key areas of depth around AI/ML/Agentic AI security, cloud security, data platform security, hybrid solutions and operating securely at scale.
  • Excellent collaboration, influencing, negotiation, coaching and coalition-building skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience developing security architecture using agile methodology.
  • Experience in AI security architecture and practical application of AI technologies.
  • Experience with the concepts and practical application of AI security, and the future of secure autonomous systems.
  • A self-starter that is naturally inquisitive and proactive in identifying threats and emerging risks.
  • Infrastructure experience and expertise (e.g. private/public cloud)
  • Master’s or PhD. degree.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in computer science or related field.

Pay Range

The typical pay range for this role is:

$175,100.00 - $334,750.00

jobs.description:
The Company

Serving the People Who Serve the People

Granicus is driven by the excitement of building, implementing, and maintaining technology that is transforming the Govtech industry by bringing governments and its constituents together. We are on a mission to support our customers with meeting the needs of their communities and implementing our technology in ways that are equitable and inclusive. Granicus has consistently appeared on the GovTech 100 list over the past 5 years and has been recognized as the best companies to work on BuiltIn.

Over the last 25 years, we have served 5,500 federal, state, and local government agencies and more than 300 million citizen subscribers power an unmatched Subscriber Network that use our digital solutions to make the world a better place. With comprehensive cloud-based solutions for communications, government website design, meeting and agenda management software, records management, and digital services, Granicus empowers stronger relationships between government and residents across the U.S., U.K., Australia, New Zealand, and Canada. By simplifying interactions with residents, while disseminating critical information, Granicus brings governments closer to the people they serve—driving meaningful change for communities around the globe.

Want to know more? See more of what we do here.

Job Summary

The Customer Success Consultant – Strategic Accounts is a trusted advisor responsible for driving adoption, value realization, and long-term success for a focused portfolio of high-value strategic customers. These customers receive a more personalized and proactive level of service, including Strategic Review meetings every six months, collaborative Success Planning, and in-person engagements.

This role is ideal for professionals with a strong background in customer success, account management, or consulting, particularly those who thrive in high-touch, relationship-driven environments. You will work closely with strategic clients to align Granicus solutions with their evolving goals, ensuring they achieve measurable outcomes and remain long-term partners.

What Success Looks Like

You treat every customer interaction as a chance to learn something you didn't know — about their goals, their organization, their industry. You build intimacy with customers through proactive outreach, and you think ahead on their goals and how we can help them get there — often before they've had to ask. You're comfortable asking “why” past the first answer, and you're genuinely curious about how customers actually use the product, not just whether they say they're satisfied with it.

What Your Impact Will Look Like

  • Essential Functions

    Strategic Customer Engagement

    • Serve as a dedicated strategic advisor to a smaller, high-impact book of business.
    • Conduct Strategic Review meetings every six months with each customer to assess progress, align on goals, and identify new opportunities.
    • Develop and maintain shared Success Plans that outline customer objectives, key milestones, and success metrics.
    • Build deep relationships through in-office visits, conference attendance, and tradeshow engagements as needed.

    Customer Success Management & Strategy

    • Act as the primary point of contact for strategic customers, ensuring a seamless experience across onboarding, adoption, and renewal.
    • Collaborate cross-functionally with Sales, Implementation, and Support to resolve issues and deliver value.
    • Analyze customer usage data and engagement metrics to inform proactive outreach and strategic recommendations.
    • Proactively surface risk and opportunity signals before they show up in a health score — through usage patterns, organizational changes, or conversations that go beyond the stated agenda.
    • Monitor customer health and implement mitigation strategies to reduce churn risk.

    Growth & Expansion

    • Identify and nurture expansion opportunities through consultative conversations and strategic planning.
    • Ask questions beyond the immediate request — the best expansion opportunities usually surface from understanding what the customer is trying to solve, not just what they explicitly asked for.
    • Partner with Sales to co-develop account growth strategies and support upsell/cross-sell initiatives.
    • Present tailored value propositions to executive stakeholders.
    • Ability/experience in ability to assist in RFP response process as well as to present in a finalist capacity to a customer

    Customer Advocacy & Experience

    • Champion the voice of the customer internally, advocating for product enhancements and service improvements.
    • Contribute to customer reference programs and success story development.
    • Stay current on Granicus product updates, industry trends, and best practices in customer success.

    Customer Success Operations

    • Maintain accurate and up-to-date records in CRM and customer success platforms.
    • Follow standardized processes while contributing to continuous improvement initiatives.
    Track and report on key performance indicators, including engagement, satisfaction, and retention.

You Will Love This Job If You Have

Requirements:

  • 3–5+ years of experience in customer success, account management, or consulting, preferably with strategic or enterprise clients.
  • Proven ability to manage executive relationships and lead strategic planning conversations.
  • Demonstrated track record of identifying and acting on opportunities without being prompted — able to give a specific example of surfacing an expansion, a risk, or a process improvement before someone else flagged it.
  • Genuine curiosity — comfortable asking “why” past the first answer, and interested in how customers actually use the product, not just whether they're satisfied with it.
  • Strong analytical skills and comfort with data-driven decision-making.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills.
  • Experience with CRM systems (Salesforce preferred) and customer success tools.
  • Willingness to travel up to 25% for client meetings, conferences, and events.
  • Familiarity with public sector organizations is a plus.

AI Skills & Capabilities

Required level: AI-Fluent User (Foundational, Level 3). Actively and independently uses AI tools to accelerate day-to-day work — synthesizing account usage data ahead of Strategic Reviews, drafting and refining Success Plans, and preparing for customer conversations. Comfortable writing a clear, specific prompt and iterating on the output, and applies healthy judgment to verify AI-assisted work rather than taking it at face value.

  • Uses AI-assisted tools as part of normal account prep — not a novelty, a working habit.
  • Can identify where AI genuinely saves time on repetitive account work (data synthesis, drafting, summarization) versus where it doesn't fit.
  • Preferred, not required: experience building a repeatable AI-assisted workflow or template that others on the team have adopted (Power User level — Intermediate, Levels 4–5) — a plus for candidates who've gone beyond ad hoc use, but not a bar every candidate needs to clear.

Performance Metrics

  • Strategic Review completion rate and quality
  • Success Plan adoption and alignment with customer goals
  • Customer satisfaction and Net Promoter Score (NPS)
  • Retention and renewal rates
  • Product adoption and usage growth
  • Expansion revenue and opportunity identification
  • Ratio of rep-initiated to customer-initiated strategic conversations — a proxy for proactive vs. reactive engagement, measurable off existing cadence tracking.

Travel Requirements

  • Up to 25% domestic (and potential international) travel for in-person client meetings, conferences, and strategic engagements.

Security Requirement:

Responsible for Granicus information security by appropriately preserving the Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA) of Granicus information assets in accordance with the company's information security program.

EEO Statement

We are an EEO Employer. It has been and will continue to be a fundamental policy of Granicus not to discriminate on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, gender, gender identity, pregnancy, marital status, partnership status, domestic violence victim status, sexual orientation, age, national origin, citizenship status, veteran or military status, disability, medical condition, genetic information, caregiver status or any other characteristic prohibited by federal, state and/or local laws.

About Us

Don’t have all the skills/experience mentioned above? At Granicus, we are trying to build diverse, inclusive teams. We do not have degree requirements for most of our roles. If you don’t meet every requirement above but are excited to learn more, we encourage you to apply. We might just be able to find another role that could be a perfect fit!

Security and Privacy Requirements

  • Responsible for Granicus information security by appropriately preserving the Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA) of Granicus information assets in accordance with the company's information security program.
  • Responsible for ensuring the data privacy of our employees and customers, their data, as well as taking all required privacy training in a timely manner, in accordance with company policies.

  • We are a remote-first company with a globally distributed workforce across the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, India, Armenia, Australia, and New Zealand.

Application Security Engineer

Parallels is seeking a highly motivated and talented Application Security Engineer to join our team. Your primary responsibility will be to coordinate with more senior members of our team to write exploits and design fixes for existing application vulnerabilities. You will also help search for new critical/high risk vulnerabilities in our codebase. In addition, you will assist in vulnerability disclosure processes and help implement repeatable secure development practices.

As issues are uncovered, you will communicate with the appropriate technical and leadership teams to ensure a focus on risk mitigation – allowing for business continuity, but without negligent risk. Application security engineers are constantly assessing applications for weaknesses and finding resolutions before they can be abused.

This is the moment.It's an exciting time at Parallels — strong leadership, a refreshed brand, and a whole new approach to how the world works. The EUC market is shifting fast, and we're at the front of that wave. We want you riding it with us.

We want you to be you.Too many companies tell you about their culture and then expect you to fit it. Ours is built from the people who work here. We want you to feel safe being who you are, taking risks, and showing us what you've got.

We are seeking a Senior Site Reliability Engineer with strong Microsoft Azure experience to help operate, scale, and improve the reliability of our critical cloud-based services. This role will anchor an SRE Team that will focus on production reliability, observability, automation, incident response, cloud operations, and continuous improvement.

The Sr. SRE partners with software engineering, product, security, and operations leadership to embed reliability principles into the software delivery lifecycle, mentors the SRE team, and serves as the technical authority for observability and reliability across mission‐critical healthcare workloads.

Role and Responsibilities

Reliability Engineering

·Define, implement, and improve Service Level Indicators, Service Level Objectives, and error budgets for critical applications and platform services.

  • Identify and eliminate recurring reliability issues through root cause analysis, automation, and architectural improvements.

  • Participate in production readiness reviews for new services, major releases, and infrastructure changes.

Observability and Monitoring

  • Build and improve observability across applications, infrastructure, networks, and cloud services. Implement monitoring for the four golden signals of Latency, Traffic, Errors, and Saturation

  • Analyze system performance, bottlenecks, saturation trends, and capacity risks.

  • Improve backup, disaster recovery, failover, and business continuity practices.

  • Partner with engineering teams to implement resiliency patterns such as retries, circuit breakers, bulkheads, graceful degradation, and queue-based decoupling.

  • Support and improve production workloads running on Microsoft Azure.

  • Collaborate with cloud and network teams on secure, scalable Azure architecture.

  • Help enforce Azure operational standards, including tagging, monitoring, backup, recovery, identity, security, and cost awareness.

Security and Compliance Support

  • Support operational controls for identity, access, encryption, secrets management, vulnerability remediation, logging, and auditability.

  • Proven track record designing and rolling out an SLO program with SLIs, SLOs, and error budget policy in production environments.

  • Observability Tools: Hands-on experience with enterprise observability platform such as Datadog and Dynatrace, Elastic, Grafana, Prometheus or LogicMonitor.

  • Prior experience standing up or anchoring an SRE practice, including operating model, rituals, and adoption across multiple engineering teams.

  • Strong incident command experience and a track record of running blameless postmortems that drive measurable improvement.

  • Healthcare IT experience and familiarity with HIPAA, HITRUST, or equivalent compliance frameworks.

  • Multi‐cloud reliability experience (AWS) in addition to Azure.

  • Chaos engineering and resiliency testing experience (e.g., Gremlin, Chaos Mesh, Azure Chaos Studio).

  • Infrastructure as Code expertise (Terraform, Bicep, Ansible) for observability and remediation automation.

  • Scripting and programming proficiency (Python, PowerShell, Go) for automation, tooling, and integration work.

  • Experience with security controls, vulnerability management, compliance audits, and cloud governance.

  • Recognized industry certifications (e.g., Azure Solutions Architect, Google SRE certificate, CKA).

Position

Title: Sr. Performance Consultant – Digital Experience (DEX) and SaaS Transitions

Location: United States (Remote, with customer travel as required)

Clearance Level: TS/SCI

Technology Specialization: Digital Experience Management

The Performance Consultant is a senior individual contributor and subject matter expert within Riverbed Professional Services, focused on delivering Aternity‑based Digital Experience (DEX) solutions in SaaS environments.

This role supports enterprise and US secured customers by leading complex DEX deployments, SaaS operations, and on‑prem to SaaS transitions.   • Strong customer-facing skills with the ability to engage credibly at senior and executive levels.

Our employee benefits including flexible workplace policies, employee resource groups, learning and development resources, career progression pathways, and community engagement initiatives are some of the reasons why we have had great success in bringing in new talent.
